transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm here because flying has started to feel way scarier than it really should. Um, just the idea of getting on a plane makes me picture that turbulence from my honeymoon flight all over again. I mean, I know people fly safely every single day, but it's just really getting to me.
Do you find yourself having unwanted, distressing memories or nightmares about that flight on your honeymoon?

No, not really. I don't have nightmares about it or anything like that. It's just when I actually have to think about getting on a plane, or if I'm booking a ticket, that's when I get really anxious and remember how bad it felt. But it doesn't just pop into my head when I'm going about my normal day.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things in your daily life, such as your health, finances, or work, even when you aren't thinking about flying?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, I have the normal amount of stress from work and everyday stuff, but it's nothing excessive. I don't really worry about things all the time or anything like that. It's honestly just the flying that makes me feel this anxious.
Do you currently avoid flying or travel by other means to prevent feeling that anxiety?

Yeah, I definitely try to avoid it. If I can, I'll choose to drive, even if it's a really long trip, or I'll just turn down work trainings that require me to fly. And if I absolutely have to plan a trip or even just talk about one, I need my husband sitting right there with me. Otherwise, I'll just back out of it completely.
When you are in a situation where you must fly, do you feel an immediate, intense surge of fear or panic that feels out of proportion to the actual danger of the flight?

Yeah, I definitely do. It's really fast. Like, if I’m just looking at flights for a conference, or sometimes even if I just hear a plane overhead, my chest tightens right away. I get this sudden rush of panic, and I feel like I just need to shut the laptop or get away from the thought completely. So, yes, it's a very immediate reaction.
